Review of the library prompt (LIBRARY_CATALOG) and of SUITE_CHAT's KEEPS how-to pattern
=========================================================================================
Branch wip-2026-11-24-library. Asked to review 0035cea; the branch moved while I worked (6389953 OPEN read only as a
line of its own, 4d04d77 and 08959b4 recalibrated SURETY on 624 and 924 questions). Everything below is at 08959b4
unless it says 0035cea. I did not write any of this change. Nothing in src/ was changed.

  node tests/fixtures/review_library_1238/replay.js [path/to/lantern.inner.html]

At 08959b4:  423 cases: 299 AGREE, 124 DISAGREE  (disagree: high 32, medium 45, low 47)
At 0035cea:  423 cases: 304 AGREE, 119 DISAGREE  (the OPEN and "numbers" differences are in 6 and 9 below)

  keeps  147 cases, 57 disagree (32 through HEALTH_CHAT, 14 through SUITE_PASSAGES, 11 nothing given)
  open    89 cases, 34 disagree
  header 125 cases, 17 disagree
  prompt  62 cases, 16 disagree

How each part is judged is in the head of cases.js. "keeps" runs Chat's lesson providers in their own order after the
safety rule, as ASSIST_CHAT does, with the usual prompt: what the model is really handed, not only S.passages.


1. HIGH. KEEPS also reaches HEALTH_CHAT, which hands WRONG Health lessons whole, in every prompt mode
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The KEEPS comment says the lesson "is still given only when it is sure to be about the question (SUITE_PASSAGES)".
That holds for SUITE_CHAT's own provider, but not for HEALTH_CHAT's: its provider is FIRST in Lantern.chatContext
(CTX.unshift), and Lantern.healthLessons(q) calls lessons(q, false) whenever S.chat.howTo(q) is true. That path's bar
is the best Health lesson with strong >= 1 or cover >= 0.5 -- one shared word ("after", "tank", "fridge", "drink")
clears it -- and the lesson goes WHOLE, with "(Lantern: this is a health question, so Lantern sent its Health lesson
whole. Give the steps to do now, in order, and say when to get a health worker.)". Before KEEPS none of these
questions got any lesson. Seen through CHAT.converse with a stand-in model, in the auto, short and library prompts:

  How long can medicine be kept after the expiry date?     -> Just born: the first hour after birth; Shock
  How long do pills last after they expire?                -> the same two
  How long can ORS be kept after mixing?                   -> Shock; the afterbirth lesson
                                                              (Oral rehydration says "make it fresh each day": not given)
  How long can insulin / vaccines be kept out of the fridge? -> Keeping food without a fridge
  How long can I keep my pills in a hot car?               -> Caring for a sick person; Too hot, too cold
  Is it safe to drink alcohol with antibiotics?            -> Making water safe to drink; Enough water
  Is it safe to drink alcohol while taking paracetamol?    -> the same
  Is it safe to drink sea water if I boil it?              -> Making water safe ("Boil (safest)") -- boiling leaves
                                                              the salt; a model answering from it says yes
  Is it safe to drink bleach?                              -> Making water safe ("about 2 drops per litre"), not Poisoning
  Is it safe to drink water from a car radiator?           -> Making water safe, Enough water
  How long does diesel keep in a tank?                     -> Enough water; Drowning
  How long can I keep a car running in a closed garage?    -> Caring for a sick person (the answer is never: CO)
  Is it safe to eat mouldy bread if I cut the mould off?   -> the two water lessons
  Is it safe to eat green potatoes?                        -> Eating well on little (potato as a staple)
  ... and 18 more in cases.js (keeps-*, "health-need:" in the replay's DISAGREE lines).

No lesson on shelf 6 holds a dose figure (I scanned all 67), so no dose reaches the model this way; but a medicine
question is answered "from" a lesson about babies, food or water, under an instruction to give the steps to do now.
Rule 7: Lantern changed what the model sees on a guess. Two ways out, for whoever mends it:
  - HEALTH_CHAT's how-to path keeps the how-to test it had (no KEEPS), or asks sure() of SUITE_PASSAGES as well; and
  - a question that names a medicine (insulin, vaccine, pills, tablets, antibiotics, paracetamol, medicine ...) gets no
    lesson by KEEPS at all: Lantern has none about keeping or mixing medicines.

2. HIGH. Through SUITE_PASSAGES too, "safe to eat X" finds a lesson on making FOOD safe, for things that are not food
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KEEPS reads "is it safe to eat/drink X" and passages() finds the food-safety lesson; that lesson assumes X is food.
  Is it safe to eat wild mushrooms?            -> Cooking food so it is safe (cooking does not make a poisonous one safe)
  What wild plants are safe to eat?            -> Cooking food so it is safe
  Is it safe to eat meat from a sick goat?     -> Cooking food first ("71 C"); Illness: signs & action, which says
                                                  "Never eat an animal that died of an unknown illness", third
  Is it safe to eat a chicken that died on its own? -> Chickens & eggs first, Illness third
  Is it safe to eat raw cassava?               -> with Eating well on little (cassava as a staple to eat every day)
  Is it safe to eat fish from a polluted river? -> Cooking food (cooking does not remove pollution)
  How long can paint be kept once opened?      -> the Draw tile's help guide
  How long does honey last?                    -> Feeding babies and children (no honey before 12 months)
  How long can a baby be left alone?           -> Feeding babies and children
And food questions get the lesson for a different case, with a figure a small model will copy:
  How long can raw meat be kept without refrigeration? -> Keeping food without a fridge, whose only time is "eat it
      within about two weeks" (DRIED meat); the 2-hour rule (Keeping food and water safe, Cooking food) is not given
  How long can leftovers be kept in the fridge?        -> Keeping food WITHOUT a fridge, whose only fridge figure is
      "kept cold in a fridge they last for months" (a ferment)
Rule 7 asks what else the thing can be (a poison, a sick or dead animal, a medicine, a fuel) before handing a lesson.

3. HIGH. The header claims shelves it should not, and in the sure words when the surety is "likely"
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
a) header() says "This question is on shelf X. Lantern has opened it for you" whenever a how-to's lessons are given
   (r.given), whatever the band. lesson-howto measures 43 in 52 (83%, "likely"), and the model is meant to see the
   word the measure gives. Every wrong lesson of 1 and 2 above becomes a SURE claim:
     Is it safe to drink alcohol with antibiotics?  "This question is on shelf 6.3 safe water."
     How long can insulin / vaccines be kept out of the fridge?  "... on shelf 6.1 health and first aid"
     Is it safe to eat wild mushrooms?              "... on shelf 6.2 food"
   On the questions I wrote to probe KEEPS, the lesson-howto claim was right for 13 of 21 -- a chosen sample, not a
   calibration, but it says the 83% was not measured on questions like these.
b) Recipe cards that Assist matches by one word give "most likely" claims (card-one, 88%):
     Who wrote the book Things Fall Apart?          -> 6.4 farming and animals ("fall": plants-bed card)
     A robot faces north, turns right twice then left once. Which way does it face? -> 9.3 places (place-bearing)
     How do I find north without a compass?         -> 9.3, with the bearing card between two places
     A 5 m ladder leans on a wall 4 m up. How far is its foot from the wall? -> 9.3 ("how far": place-distance)
   The card choice is old (A.match); naming it to the model as the shelf Lantern opened is new. At 0035cea these
   were SURE (card-one was 90%).
c) How long can paint be kept once opened? -> "most likely on shelf 9.2 drawings, pictures and charts" and the
   drawing block (kindOf is "make": "paint").

4. MEDIUM. Keeping food without a fridge is on the health shelf
-----------------------------------------------------------------
health_food (Keeping food without a fridge) takes its shelf from its tile, Health, so food questions are claimed
"on shelf 6.1 health and first aid (never a dose)": leftovers in the fridge, cooked beans, milk, raw meat. The
catalog already moves health_water and health_waterstore to 6.3 by LESSON; by the catalog's own titles health_food
belongs on 6.2 ("food: cooking, keeping and eating well"), and so may health_nutrition (Eating well on little, the
same title as food_thrift on 6.2).

5. MEDIUM. The header says one thing and Chat sends another
-------------------------------------------------------------
route() reads Lantern.healthLessons only for a health NEED; HEALTH_CHAT also gives lessons for a how-to (1). So the
library prompt says "Lantern has no lesson it is sure of for this question ... you may reply OPEN" and the same turn
carries Health lessons: mouldy bread, medicine after expiry, pills in a hot car, diesel, potatoes, yoghurt, a car in
a garage, how long labour lasts (14 of the questions I tried; prompt-consistent-*).

6. MEDIUM. Assist is told about OPEN and lessons it never runs or sends
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Lantern.assistPromptWrap puts Chat's header on Assist's prompt. Assist (A.solve) runs no Chat command and gives no
lessons, yet its library prompt says "reply with only one line: OPEN 5.4" or "Lantern has opened it for you: its
lessons come with the question" or "its catalog comes with the question". A stand-in reply "OPEN 6.1" ended Assist
after one round with "OPEN 6.1" as its text and no answer (What causes earthquakes?, the rice question). The Courier
(copy the prompt to any AI) carries the same lines. For Assist the header could be the shelf line alone, without
OPEN and without "come with the question".

7. MEDIUM. OPEN: the forms a small model copies from the prompt are not read (at 08959b4)
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The header lists other shelves as "6.2 food: cooking, keeping and eating well" and the start lists classes as
"6 health, food, water and farming". What stands after a line to copy is copied with it (CLAUDE.md, 1.24.6), and
these are not read now; the reply then goes to the person as the answer:
  OPEN 6.2 food: cooking, keeping and eating well     OPEN 6 health, food, water and farming
  OPEN 6.2 (food: cooking, keeping and eating well)   OPEN 6.2 food      `OPEN 6.2`      ANSWER: OPEN 6.2
0035cea read the first four; 6389953 dropped them to stop "Open 2 windows". Both can hold: after the number, allow
words only when they are the start of that shelf's or class's own title (or brackets, backticks, an ANSWER: label),
and refuse any other word. Still read wrongly in both versions: an OPEN line inside a list of steps in capitals --
"Valve sequence: / CLOSE 1 / OPEN 2 / CLOSE 3" is read as class 2 (money), "OPEN 1 / PUMP 3 TIMES" as class 1,
"OPEN 2.5 / turns of the valve" as shelf 2.5 (none) -- and the answer is thrown away. An OPEN line beside other
step lines (CLOSE, PUMP, numbered steps) is not a request. Low: "open 6.2", "OPEN Shelf 6.2", "OPEN CLASS 6",
"- OPEN 6.2", "OPEN 6.2, 6.1", a no-break space.

8. MEDIUM. What OPEN sends has no "sure" bar
---------------------------------------------
open() sends the two best lessons on the shelf whatever their score: OPEN 6.1 for "How long can insulin be kept out
of the fridge?" sends Keeping food without a fridge and Pregnancy; for "How long can I keep antibiotics?" Keeping
food and the recovery position; for "Is it safe to drink bleach?" Burns before Poisoning. When nothing on the shelf
is about the question it could say so ("Shelf 6.1 has nothing more for this question", as it already does for a
shelf with no lessons).

9. LOW to MEDIUM. Suggestions ("may be on shelf X ... OPEN X") that name the wrong shelf
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"Compose a short march in G major." -> 0.1 Lantern's own tiles (music is 9.1; Chat does not see a song in it);
"Write HELLO in Morse code." -> 0.1; "Write the word LANTERN in the NATO alphabet." -> 3.1 (MORSE and NATO are on 3.3);
"Why is the sky blue?" -> 5.2. A guess named is a guess copied (the module's own comment).
Fixed between 0035cea and 08959b4: "most likely on shelf 4.1 arithmetic" for questions whose only number is not a
sum ("twice a day", "a 2 year old", "for 2 days", "family of 6", "at 3000 m") -- "numbers" is now 34% and names
nothing.

10. LOW. KEEPS misses the commonest ways to ask (nothing given where a lesson answers)
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
"How long is cooked rice good for?", "Can I eat rice that was left out overnight?", "Should I throw away chicken left
out all night?", "How long can I store drinking water?" ("stored" is in the list, "store" is not), "Is it safe to
give honey to a baby?", sauerkraut with white scum, a tourniquet, petrol, a generator indoors. And any digit stops
howTo(): "How long can cooked rice be left out at 30 degrees?" gets nothing, though the lesson's "1 hour when it is
hotter than 32 C" is exactly what is asked (medium). These are gaps, not harm: no lesson is better than a wrong one.

What is right (the AGREE cases, kept as a guard)
-------------------------------------------------
- KEEPS gives the right lesson for cooked food left out (the bench's rice row and 13 variants, curly apostrophe, em
  dash, capitals), raw milk, raw eggs, pink pork, cracked eggs, bulging cans, dried, salted and smoked food,
  ferments, jam, seeds, water from rain, rivers, streams, puddles, floods and near latrines, and how long to keep
  pressing a wound, cooling a burn, pushing in CPR, or leaving someone in the recovery position.
- Every medicine question with a dose word goes to the medicine rule first; no lesson on shelf 6 holds a dose.
- The library prompt keeps the short instructions whole, in Chat (30 questions) and Assist (8): nothing dropped or
  garbled; it only adds the fixed start and the header.
- OPEN is read only with the library prompt; "OPEN 6.2", "OPEN: 6.2", "**OPEN 6.2**", "OPEN shelf 6.2", "OPEN 6",
  a fence, a think block, Windows line ends; not in a sentence, nor "Open 2 windows", nor "OPEN 10" or "OPEN 6.21".
- Sums, drawings, circuits, code, music, slides, health needs and repair how-tos are named on the right shelf (108 of
  125 header cases agree).

Not tested: any real model (the cases are what Lantern does with a question or a reply, and stand-in replies); the
encyclopedia (0.2) with a library present; Text Reader with a document attached; the bench.
